note: Posts only we can make, because only we have counted. Every number is COUNTED not estimated, and the question is always the opinion half — we supply the fact, the reader supplies the verdict. A post that asserts what a number MEANS is the slop law again.

posts.text:
Charizard has 62 cards.

52 Pokémon have exactly one.

Out of 16,468 English cards. Too many, or about right?
posts.why: Counted across the whole catalogue. The comparison is the post.

posts.text:
16,468 English cards. 1,244 different Pokémon and forms.

That's 13.2 cards each on average.

Pikachu has 118. Fair?
posts.why: An average nobody has computed, and a leader most people would guess wrong.

posts.text:
52 Pokémon have exactly one card across every English set we track.

Name one you think deserves more.
posts.why: A permission question by construction — obscure is the only possible answer.

posts.text:
377 different people have drawn a Pokémon card.

The most prolific has 938: Ken Sugimori.

How many could you name?
posts.why: Counted, and studios excluded — 5ban Graphics has 1,386 credits and is not a person. The honest answer for almost everyone is one or two, which is the reply.

posts.text:
Most-printed type across every English card: Water, 1,931 cards.

Rarest: Fairy, 194.

Surprised?
posts.why: From the printed type field, not video-game typing — those differ, and the difference has already caught us once.
